summary: The main article describes a visible-light-induced enantioselective b-amination of a,b-unsaturated 2-acyl imidazoles using a chiral-at-rhodium Lewis acid catalyst. The document includes optimization tables, mechanistic schemes, and scope figures for various substrates and carbamates.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Formation of C -N bonds by b -amination of readily available a , b -unsaturated carbonyl compounds. Scope limitations for the PCET-induced radical coupling reported in this study: X ¼ aryl, Y ¼ CO2R, R 1 ¼ aryl, R 2 ¼ 2-imidazolyl.
items.description: This figure illustrates the general strategy for conjugate amination and the specific scope limitations of the PCET-induced radical coupling method.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the reaction conditions a
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of catalysts, bases, photoredox mediators, and solvents to optimize the yield and enantioselectivity of the b-amination reaction.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Proposed mechanism.
items.description: A detailed catalytic cycle showing the proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and the subsequent radical-radical coupling controlled by the rhodium catalyst.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Control experiments.
items.description: This figure shows experimental evidence for the nitrogen-centered radical intermediate and other mechanistic control studies.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Reaction scope with regards to 2-acyl imidazoles.
items.description: This figure displays the variety of a,b-unsaturated 2-acyl imidazole substrates that are compatible with the optimized reaction conditions.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: Reaction scope with respect to carbamates. a No desired product formed but instead a cyclobutane side product.
items.description: This figure explores the compatibility of different carbamate nucleophiles, including various O-substituents and N-aryl groups.

items.heading: Fig. 6
items.caption: Follow-up chemistry with a cross-coupling reaction product 3m .
items.description: Demonstrates the synthetic utility of the products by converting 3m into a chiral b-amino acid ester derivative.
